points.t: An **expanding red (or bluish) patch** days to weeks after outdoor exposure; central clearing optional; usually not hot or itchy.
*Borrelia burgdorferi* sensu lato from an **Ixodes tick**: dermal spread (EM) or chronic infection (ACA, mainly *B. afzelii*).
EM: **doxycycline 100 mg BD (or 200 mg OD) for 21 days**. No blood test for typical EM (NICE NG95).
**Carditis, meningitis / encephalitis, uveitis**, facial palsy with neurology. No test or antibiotics after an asymptomatic bite.

cause.lead: A tick passes Borrelia into the skin.
points: Ticks in woodland, moorland, long grass, parks (Scotland, south England, Lake District, Europe, N. America).
Transmission rises with attachment time: **remove early**.
EM appears **3 days–3 months** after the bite (commonly 1–4 weeks); many don’t recall a bite.
Late: **ACA** on extensor limbs of older people (European exposure).

visuals.caption: Remove a tick with fine-tipped tweezers or a tick tool: grasp close to the skin and pull steadily upwards; don’t twist, crush, burn or smother it.
visuals.alt: Tweezers lifting a tick straight up from skin

features.lead: A rash that grows, not one that flares and fades.
points: **Enlarging red rash**, often ≥ 5 cm, at the bite site (legs, groin, axillae, beltline; head / neck in children).
Central clearing (‘bull’s-eye’) is **optional**; many lesions are uniformly red or bluish.
Usually **not** hot, itchy or painful; ± flu-like symptoms.
**Not EM**: a hot itchy reaction that appears within hours and fades by 48 h (bite hypersensitivity).
**ACA**: bluish-red doughy limb → thin ‘cigarette-paper’ skin with visible veins; ± neuropathy.

visuals.caption: Erythema migrans enlarges day by day from the bite. Drawing round the edge (dashed rings) shows the spread; central clearing may or may not appear.
visuals.alt: Expanding red ring on an arm with pen-marked edges

points: **Diagnose and treat clinically**; early serology often negative.
**ELISA then immunoblot** via a UKAS-accredited lab.
Test after an asymptomatic bite; use unaccredited private panels.

cards.name: Tick-bite hypersensitivity
cards.clue: Within hours, fades ≤ 48 h, itchy / hot, small.

cards.name: Tinea corporis
cards.clue: Scaly active edge; EM is not scaly.

cards.name: Granuloma annulare
cards.clue: Chronic firm papular ring; no daily expansion.

cards.name: ACA mimics
cards.clue: Chilblains, venous disease, morphoea, ageing skin.

manage.lead: NICE NG95: adults and ≥ 12 years with EM, no focal symptoms.

points: Cover skin, repellent, check folds and scalp after outdoors.
Remove ticks per UKHSA (tweezers / tick tool, pull steadily).
**No prophylactic antibiotics or serology** after an asymptomatic bite; watch the site for weeks.

rx.dose: 100 mg twice daily or 200 mg once daily
rx.note: Upright with water; separate from antacids / iron / calcium; sun protection; avoid in pregnancy and < 12.
Usually used in pregnancy after assessment.

points: Children < 12 (and some < 18), focal disease, ACA: per NG95 / specialist.

limits.t: No more antibiotics: specialist / reference-lab advice.

items.t: Meningitis / encephalitis signs, carditis or heart block, uveitis.
Facial palsy, radiculopathy, inflammatory arthritis, multiple EM with systemic upset: discuss with specialist **without delaying antibiotics**.

pearls.t: **Expanding red ring after the outdoors = treat. Don’t test.**
The full **21 days** matters for EM.
Reinfection is possible; no lasting immunity.
ACA is missed as ‘poor circulation’ in older limbs: ask about European countryside.

quiz.a: Doxycycline 100 mg BD or 200 mg OD for 21 days.

quiz.q: Antibiotics after an asymptomatic tick bite?
Red itchy patch that appeared within hours and faded by 48 h?
